name: The Churchill Arms
description: One of London's most photographed pubs, covered in flowers outside and filled with Churchill memorabilia inside. Also serves excellent Thai food.
tips: The exterior is spectacular in summer. The Thai food at the back is surprisingly good and cheap.

name: Ye Olde Cheshire Cheese
description: A historic pub rebuilt in 1667 after the Great Fire. Former haunt of Dickens, Dr. Johnson, and Mark Twain. Atmospheric dark wood and low ceilings.
tips: Explore all the nooks and levels. The cellar bar dates to the 13th century.

name: The Lamb and Flag
description: One of London's oldest pubs (1623), tucked down an alley in Covent Garden. Charles Dickens was a regular.
tips: Nicknamed the 'Bucket of Blood' due to historic bare-knuckle fights. Great pre-theatre pint.

name: Callooh Callay
description: Award-winning cocktail bar inspired by Lewis Carroll. There's a secret bar hidden behind a wardrobe. Quirky, creative cocktails.
tips: Ask about the hidden bar through the wardrobe.

name: The Mayor of Scaredy Cat Town
description: A hidden speakeasy accessed through a vintage Smeg fridge door in a breakfast cafe. Quirky cocktails in a cosy underground space.
tips: Say 'I'm here to see the Mayor' to be shown to the fridge door entrance.

name: Nightjar
description: One of the world's top cocktail bars. Live jazz and vintage-style cocktails served with theatrical flair in a 1920s setting.
tips: Reservations essential. The live music is excellent. Each cocktail is a theatrical experience.

name: Ronnie Scott's Jazz Club
description: London's legendary jazz club since 1959. World-class musicians perform in an intimate Soho basement setting.
tips: Book the late show for a cheaper, more intimate experience.

name: The Prospect of Whitby
description: London's oldest riverside pub (1520) with a flagstone floor, pewter bar, and stunning Thames views from the terrace.
tips: Grab a spot on the riverside terrace at sunset.

name: The Blues Kitchen Shoreditch
description: Live blues, soul, and rock 'n' roll every night with free entry. American BBQ food and bourbon cocktails.
tips: Free live music every night! Great BBQ ribs too.

name: Gordon's Wine Bar
description: London's oldest wine bar, hidden in a candlelit cave beneath the Embankment. Atmospheric and romantic.
tips: Cash only inside! Arrive early to get a spot in the cave.

name: The George Inn
description: London's last surviving galleried coaching inn, now owned by the National Trust. Shakespeare drank here.
tips: The courtyard is magical in summer. Right next to Borough Market.

name: Fabric
description: Iconic nightclub in a former meat cold store. Three rooms of electronic music with the legendary 'bodysonic' dancefloor.
tips: The bodysonic dancefloor in Room 1 is unique. Opens late, goes until morning.

name: The Faltering Fullback
description: A beloved locals' pub with a magical multi-level beer garden that feels like a treehouse. Great for sports.
tips: The beer garden is like a jungle gym for adults. Great for watching sports.

name: Swift Soho
description: Two-floor cocktail bar: upstairs for a quick drink, downstairs for serious cocktail connoisseurs.
tips: Downstairs is the star — book a table. The Irish Coffee is one of London's best.

name: The Holly Bush
description: A charming Georgian pub in the heart of Hampstead village. Cosy wood-panelled rooms, real ales, and a traditional pub feel.
tips: Combine with a walk on Hampstead Heath. The Sunday roast is excellent.

name: The Dog & Duck
description: A beautiful Victorian pub in the heart of Soho. Ornate tiles, etched glass, and real ales. George Orwell and Madonna have both been regulars.
tips: Tiny pub — arrive early for a spot. The Victorian interior is worth seeing alone.

name: The Sun Tavern
description: Bethnal Green craft cocktail bar specialising in Irish whiskey and creative cocktails. Lively, unpretentious, with regular live music.
tips: The Irish whiskey selection is incredible. Live music and DJs on weekends.

name: Printworks London
description: A massive industrial nightlife venue in a former printing factory. Enormous main hall with world-class DJs, light shows, and immersive experiences.
tips: An incredible space — the scale is breathtaking. Check lineup in advance. Perfect for group nights out.

name: The World's End
description: A massive Camden institution right at the top of the high street. Three floors of drinking, live music upstairs, and a legendary beer garden.
tips: The giant clock on the exterior is a Camden landmark. Live bands upstairs most nights.

name: The Dove
description: A beautiful 18th-century riverside pub in Hammersmith. Holds the Guinness Record for the smallest bar room. Stunning Thames terrace.
tips: The riverside terrace at sunset is magical. One of London's most romantic pubs.

name: The Spaniards Inn
description: A legendary 16th-century pub on the edge of Hampstead Heath. Dickens, Keats, and Byron all drank here. Beautiful garden.
tips: Walk across Hampstead Heath to get here. The garden is one of London's best. Dick Turpin reportedly drank here.

name: Oriole
description: A stunning hidden cocktail bar beneath Smithfield Market. Live world music, theatrical cocktails, and three distinct 'world' themed rooms.
tips: Reservations essential. The live music changes nightly. Each cocktail tells a story.

name: The Blackfriar
description: London's most ornate pub — an Arts and Crafts masterpiece with gold mosaics, marble columns, and carved monks. A visual feast.
tips: The interior is jaw-droppingly beautiful. A Grade II listed building that feels like a small cathedral.

name: The Crosse Keys (Wetherspoons)
description: A JD Wetherspoons in a spectacular former banking hall. Absurdly cheap pints in one of the most beautiful rooms in the City of London.
tips: The cheapest pints in central London in one of the most impressive rooms. A quintessentially British experience.

name: 100 Club
description: Legendary live music venue since 1942. The Rolling Stones, Muddy Waters, and the Sex Pistols all played here. Still hosting incredible live music nightly.
tips: Check the lineup — incredible variety from jazz to punk to northern soul. A piece of music history.

name: Jazz Cafe
description: Intimate live music venue in Camden for jazz, soul, funk, hip-hop, and world music. The balcony tables overlooking the stage are magical.
tips: Book a balcony dinner table for the best experience — you get food + show. Saturday nights are especially lively.

name: The Glory
description: East London's most legendary LGBTQ+ bar and performance venue. Drag shows, live music, cabaret, and an incredible rooftop terrace.
tips: Check what's on — the drag shows and cabaret nights are unmissable. Very welcoming to everyone.

name: Cahoots
description: A 1940s-themed underground cocktail bar in a disused Tube station. Wartime decor, swing music, and vintage cocktails. An immersive experience.
tips: The attention to detail is incredible. Great for groups and celebrations. Book ahead.

name: Heaven
description: London's most famous nightclub, located under the arches beneath Charing Cross. Huge dancefloor, top DJs, and legendary themed nights.
address: Under the Arches, Villiers St, London WC2N 6NG
tips: Home of the legendary G-A-Y nights. Check what's on — different themed nights throughout the week.

name: The Old Bank of England
description: A magnificent Fuller's pub housed in a former Bank of England building. Soaring ceilings, chandeliers, and excellent pies in a grand Victorian banking hall.
tips: The award-winning pies are a must. The building itself is the main attraction — look up at those ceilings.

name: The Anchor Bankside
description: An 18th-century riverside pub near Shakespeare's Globe with views across the Thames to St Paul's. Samuel Pepys watched the Great Fire from here.
tips: The riverside terrace has one of the best views in London. Perfect before or after visiting the Globe.

name: The Seven Stars
description: A tiny, characterful pub behind the Royal Courts of Justice dating from 1602. Popular with barristers and legal professionals, with a resident cat.
tips: One of the few pubs to survive the Great Fire. The landlady is a legendary character. Look for the cat.

name: Ye Olde Mitre
description: A hidden gem tucked down a narrow alley in Hatton Garden, dating from 1546. One of London's most atmospheric and hard-to-find pubs.
address: 1 Ely Ct, Ely Pl, London EC1N 6SJ
tips: Genuinely hard to find — look for the alley between 8 and 9 Hatton Garden. A true hidden gem.

name: The Jerusalem Tavern
description: A tiny, atmospheric pub serving the full range of St Peter's Brewery ales. The 18th-century interior feels authentically old London.
tips: Very small — arrive early to get a seat. The St Peter's ales are excellent and unique to this pub.

name: The Flask Highgate
description: A stunning 17th-century pub in Highgate Village with a beautiful garden, real fires, and a Dick Turpin connection. Atmospheric and charming.
tips: The garden is lovely in summer. Combine with a walk through Highgate Cemetery nearby.

name: The French House
description: A legendary Soho bohemian pub where Charles de Gaulle planned the French Resistance. No pints served — only halves. A unique piece of history.
tips: They famously only serve half pints — it's tradition. The upstairs restaurant is also excellent.

name: The Grapes
description: A 16th-century riverside pub in Limehouse, part-owned by Sir Ian McKellen. Tiny, characterful, with stunning Thames views from the back terrace.
tips: Co-owned by Sir Ian McKellen! The upstairs fish restaurant is excellent. Book for the terrace.

name: The Mayflower
description: A historic pub on the site where the Pilgrim Fathers set sail for America in 1620. The only pub licensed to sell both British and American postage stamps.
tips: The rear deck overhanging the Thames is magical. Buy a stamp as a unique souvenir.

name: The Lamb
description: A beautiful Victorian pub with rare surviving 'snob screens' — etched glass partitions that let drinkers order without being seen. Charles Dickens was a regular.
tips: The snob screens are a rare Victorian survival. Lamb's Conduit Street itself is a lovely shopping street.

name: The Princess Louise
description: A breathtaking Victorian gin palace with ornate etched glass, tiled walls, and original wood partitions. One of the most beautiful pub interiors in London.
tips: A Sam Smith's pub so pints are very cheap. The interior is genuinely one of London's finest — don't miss the tiled walls.

name: The Cittie of Yorke
description: A spectacular pub with a cavernous medieval-style main hall, enormous wine vats above the bar, and intimate snug booths. Pure atmosphere.
tips: A Sam Smith's pub — cheap pints. The main hall is extraordinary. Grab one of the private booths if you can.

name: The Ten Bells
description: A beautifully restored Victorian pub in Spitalfields, infamous for its Jack the Ripper connection. Gorgeous tiled interior and excellent craft beer selection.
tips: The Victorian tiles are stunning. Opposite the old Spitalfields Market. Great for a Jack the Ripper walking tour.

name: The Old Dr Butler's Head
description: A hidden historic pub down a narrow City alley, dating from 1616. Named after a royal physician who prescribed ale as medicine.
tips: A proper hidden gem down a City alley. Busy with office workers weekday lunchtimes, quieter evenings.

name: The Harp
description: A multi-award-winning real ale pub just off Trafalgar Square. Tiny but perfectly formed, with an outstanding rotating selection of cask ales.
tips: Voted CAMRA national pub of the year. Standing room only most times but worth it for the ale selection.

name: The Nag's Head
description: A wonderfully eccentric pub hidden in a Belgravia mews. Tiny, cash-only, crammed with memorabilia, and run with iron rule by a legendary landlord.
tips: Cash only, no mobile phones, no music — just conversation. A true London original in posh Belgravia.

name: The Grenadier
description: A hidden gem down a Belgravia mews, reportedly London's most haunted pub. Former officers' mess for the Duke of Wellington's soldiers.
tips: Famously haunted by a soldier caught cheating at cards. Hard to find but worth the search.

name: The Windsor Castle
description: A classic Kensington pub with a gorgeous walled garden and separate wood-panelled rooms. One of west London's finest traditional pubs.
tips: The walled garden is one of the best pub gardens in London. The separate rooms give an old-fashioned feel.

name: The Anglesea Arms
description: A charming South Kensington gastropub with a lovely terrace. Charles Dickens was a regular, and it has been serving since 1827.
tips: The front terrace is wonderful on sunny days. The food is excellent and well-priced for the area.

name: The Eagle
description: Britain's original gastropub, opened in 1991. Still serving its legendary Mediterranean-influenced food from an open kitchen. A piece of culinary history.
tips: The original gastropub — a piece of British food history. No bookings, just turn up. The steak sandwich is legendary.

name: The Harwood Arms
description: The only Michelin-starred pub in London. Game-focused menu in a relaxed Fulham setting. Outstanding British cooking in a proper pub atmosphere.
tips: London's only Michelin-starred pub. Book well ahead for dinner. The venison scotch egg is iconic.

name: The Canton Arms
description: A brilliant neighbourhood gastropub in Stockwell with no-frills decor but outstanding Sunday roasts and daily-changing menus. A locals' favourite.
tips: The Sunday roast is widely considered one of London's best. No bookings — arrive early.

name: The Marksman
description: A Michelin-starred gastropub on Hackney Road with a brilliant ground-floor bar and upstairs dining room. The beef and barley bun is legendary.
tips: You can drink in the bar without a reservation. The beef and barley bun is a must-order.

name: The Anchor & Hope
description: A celebrated gastropub near the Old Vic theatre, known for its hearty British cooking and no-reservations policy. Always bustling and always excellent.
tips: No bookings except Sunday lunch. Perfect before or after a show at the Old Vic or Young Vic.

name: The Drapers Arms
description: A stylish Islington gastropub with a beautiful garden and excellent wine list. Relaxed Georgian elegance with seriously good British food.
tips: The garden is gorgeous in summer. The wine list is exceptional for a pub. Sunday roasts are superb.

name: The Bull & Last
description: A beloved Highgate gastropub on the edge of Hampstead Heath. Outstanding food, great ales, and a cosy fireside atmosphere in winter.
tips: Perfect after a walk on Hampstead Heath. The bar snacks alone are worth the visit.

name: Dishoom Permit Room
description: An Irani-cafe-inspired cocktail bar attached to the famous Dishoom restaurant. Spiced cocktails, chai-infused drinks, and Bollywood vibes.
address: 12 Upper St Martin's Ln, London WC2H 9FB
tips: Try the Permit Room Chai while you wait for your Dishoom table. The Negroni Chai is exceptional.

name: The Connaught Bar
description: Regularly voted the world's best bar. Art Deco elegance with tableside martini trolley service. An unforgettable luxury cocktail experience.
tips: The martini trolley experience is a must — they mix it tableside. Dress smart. Reserve in advance.

name: American Bar at The Savoy
description: One of the world's oldest cocktail bars, serving since 1893. Art Deco glamour, live piano, and classic cocktails made to perfection.
tips: Live piano every evening. Smart dress required. Try a classic like the White Lady, invented here in 1929.

name: Dukes Bar
description: The bar where Ian Fleming was inspired to create James Bond's 'shaken not stirred' martini. Intimate, refined, and home to London's strongest martinis.
tips: Limited to two martinis per person — they're that strong. Book ahead. A true James Bond experience.

name: Artesian at The Langham
description: Multi-award-winning hotel bar in the grand Langham Hotel. Theatrical cocktails with stunning presentation in a luxurious setting.
tips: Each cocktail is a work of art. Smart casual dress code. The bar itself is beautifully designed.

name: Scarfes Bar
description: A gentleman's club-style bar in the Rosewood Hotel, named after caricaturist Gerald Scarfe. Live jazz, roaring fires, and excellent cocktails.
tips: The live jazz is excellent. Gerald Scarfe's original artwork adorns the walls. Very cosy in winter by the fire.

name: Bar Termini
description: A tiny, perfect Italian-inspired cocktail bar modelled on a Roman railway station cafe. Negronis and espresso martinis made with real craft.
tips: Standing room only mostly. The Negroni is one of London's best. Perfect for a quick, excellent drink.

name: Lyaness
description: A bold South Bank cocktail bar from Ryan Chetiyawardana, with Thames views and a menu built around unique house ingredients. Creative and forward-thinking.
address: Sea Containers London, 20 Upper Ground, London SE1 9PD
tips: The Thames views are stunning. Ask the bartenders to explain the house ingredients — each tells a story.

name: Happiness Forgets
description: A cosy basement cocktail bar in Hoxton Square with a no-standing policy and focused, perfectly executed cocktails. Intimate and unpretentious.
tips: Book ahead — it's tiny and popular. No standing means you always get a seat. Proper cocktail craft.

name: Three Sheets
description: A no-frills Dalston cocktail bar focused purely on the drinks. Short menu, perfect execution, and a relaxed neighbourhood feel.
tips: No reservations needed — just walk in. The short menu means every drink is perfected. Great for Dalston pre-drinks.

name: Satan's Whiskers
description: A much-loved Bethnal Green cocktail bar with a rock 'n' roll attitude. No menu — just tell the bartender what you like and they'll create something perfect.
tips: No cocktail menu — tell the bartender your flavour preferences and trust them. They always nail it.

name: Discount Suit Company
description: A basement bar hidden beneath a City of London office building. Excellent cocktails in a relaxed, exposed-brick setting. No pretension despite the quality.
tips: Easy to walk past — look for the stairs going down. One of the City's best-kept cocktail secrets.

name: The Beaufort Bar at The Savoy
description: A jet-black and gold Art Deco bar in The Savoy, with live cabaret performances and champagne cocktails. Pure theatrical glamour.
tips: The cabaret shows are stunning. Dress up — this is full-on glamour. Different vibe to the American Bar next door.

name: Kwant
description: A North African-inspired cocktail bar in Mayfair from the team behind Nightjar. Ornate Moroccan decor, live music, and exotic cocktails.
tips: The decor is transporting — feels like stepping into Casablanca. Live music most nights. Book ahead.

name: Nine Lives
description: A sustainability-focused cocktail bar in London Bridge using zero-waste techniques. Creative drinks made from repurposed ingredients in a vibrant, colourful space.
tips: Every ingredient is used fully — even the garnishes. Great eco-friendly approach without sacrificing quality.

name: Sager + Wilde
description: A Hackney Road wine bar with an exceptional list of natural and biodynamic wines. Minimalist chic with a real neighbourhood feel.
tips: The wine list is adventurous and well-priced. Great cheese and charcuterie boards to go with it.

name: Noble Rot
description: A Bloomsbury wine bar and restaurant from the team behind the renowned wine magazine. Outstanding wine list with thoughtful British food pairings.
tips: The wine list is a masterclass. Try the sommelier's recommendation. The food is seriously good too.

name: Vinoteca King's Cross
description: A popular wine bar and shop near King's Cross station with an accessible list of 200+ wines. Perfect for pre-train drinks or a relaxed evening.
tips: Great for a glass before catching a train. The wine list is huge but staff are helpful. You can buy bottles to take home.

name: Sotheby's Wine Bar
description: A wine bar inside the famous auction house offering rare vintages alongside accessible choices. Drink surrounded by world-class art about to go to auction.
tips: Wine by the glass from incredible producers. Browse the current exhibition while you drink. A unique experience.

name: 28-50 Wine Bar
description: A modern French-inspired wine bar with an accessible Collector's List of rare wines at near-retail prices. Excellent food and knowledgeable staff.
tips: The Collector's List offers rare wines at amazing prices. Great lunch deals too.

name: Terroirs
description: A natural wine bar near Charing Cross championing small producers and organic winemakers. Rustic French bistro food and a lively, convivial atmosphere.
tips: One of the pioneers of natural wine in London. The charcuterie is excellent. Downstairs is more atmospheric.

name: Sky Garden
description: A free-to-visit rooftop garden at the top of the Walkie Talkie building with three bars and restaurants. Panoramic 360-degree views of London.
tips: Free entry but you must book a timed slot weeks in advance. The sunrise sessions are magical.

name: Madison Rooftop Bar
description: A sleek rooftop bar with unobstructed views of St Paul's Cathedral. Cocktails, food, and DJs with one of London's most iconic backdrops.
tips: The view of St Paul's dome from the terrace is breathtaking. Great for sunset drinks.

name: Netil360
description: A laid-back rooftop bar in Hackney with panoramic views of the London skyline, a hot tub, and a relaxed festival vibe. Great cocktails and street food.
tips: You can book the hot tub on the roof! Open in summer only. Great sunset spot.

name: Frank's Cafe
description: A legendary summer pop-up rooftop bar on top of a Peckham car park. Stunning sunset views, Campari spritzes, and an achingly cool crowd.
address: Peckham Levels, 95A Rye Ln, London SE15 4ST
tips: Summer only. The sunset views over London are incredible. Arrive early on sunny evenings — it gets packed.

name: The Rooftop at Trafalgar St. James
description: An elegant rooftop bar overlooking Trafalgar Square and Nelson's Column. A unique vantage point for one of London's most famous landmarks.
tips: Looking down on Trafalgar Square is a unique experience. Book ahead, especially for sunset.

name: Aviary
description: A sophisticated rooftop restaurant and terrace bar on the 10th floor with sweeping City views. Part of the Montcalm hotel in Finsbury Square.
address: Montcalm Royal London House, 22-25 Finsbury Square, London EC2A 1DX
tips: Less well-known than other rooftop bars so easier to get a table. The terrace views are excellent.

name: Bussey Rooftop Bar
description: A Peckham rooftop bar in a former cricket bat factory with panoramic city views. DJs, street food, and a creative, diverse crowd.
tips: Great DJs and a laid-back atmosphere. Open seasonally — check before visiting. The views are superb.

name: The Culpeper
description: A Spitalfields pub with a rooftop greenhouse garden growing herbs and vegetables for the kitchen. Ground floor pub, first floor restaurant, rooftop bar.
tips: Three levels — the rooftop greenhouse is magical. You can just drink at the ground floor pub too.

name: The People's Park Tavern
description: A Victoria Park gastropub with an enormous beer garden, its own microbrewery, and regular live music and events. A true community hub.
tips: The beer garden is massive and perfect for summer. Their own-brewed beers are excellent. Great after a Victoria Park walk.

name: The Edinboro Castle
description: A Camden pub with one of London's best beer gardens, complete with fairy lights, BBQ in summer, and a lovely relaxed atmosphere.
tips: The fairy-lit garden is magical in summer. BBQ food on sunny weekends. A Camden gem away from the high street.

name: The Albion
description: A handsome Georgian pub in Islington with a large, leafy walled garden. Great for families during the day and romantic in the evening.
tips: The walled garden is a hidden oasis. Sunday roasts are excellent. Feels like a country pub in London.

name: The Prince Albert
description: A Battersea Park pub with a wonderful garden overlooking the park. Great ales, pub food, and a genuine community atmosphere.
tips: Perfect after a walk in Battersea Park. The garden catches the afternoon sun beautifully.

name: The Old Ship
description: A lovely riverside pub in Hammersmith with a gorgeous Thames-side terrace. Great for watching the Boat Race and sunset drinks by the river.
tips: The riverside terrace is wonderful on sunny days. Great for the Boat Race in spring.

name: The Trafalgar Arms
description: A lively Tooting pub with a large beer garden, regular quiz nights, and a friendly neighbourhood atmosphere. Great selection of craft beers.
tips: The quiz nights are legendary. Good craft beer selection and a big garden for summer.

name: The Barrel Project
description: A craft beer paradise on the Bermondsey Beer Mile housing multiple breweries under one railway arch. Hundreds of taps and a lively weekend atmosphere.
tips: Part of the Bermondsey Beer Mile — walk between multiple breweries on a Saturday afternoon.

name: The Kernel Brewery
description: One of London's pioneering craft breweries, open on Saturdays for direct sales and tastings. Outstanding IPAs and pale ales.
address: Arch 11, Dockley Rd Industrial Estate, London SE16 3SF
tips: Open Saturdays only. The IPAs are some of London's best. Part of the Bermondsey Beer Mile walk.

name: Brew By Numbers
description: A Bermondsey taproom with a numbering system for beers that lets you track your favourites. Modern, bright space with excellent craft beer.
tips: Each beer has a number code — style and recipe. The taproom is a great spot on the Beer Mile.

name: The Craft Beer Co.
description: A craft beer mecca with 37 taps and hundreds of bottles. One of London's most impressive selections of British and international craft beer.
tips: The tap list changes constantly — check their board. Staff are knowledgeable and happy to recommend.

name: The Southampton Arms
description: A stripped-back Kentish Town pub serving only cask ales and ciders from independent British producers. No lager, no spirits, no pretension.
tips: Cask ale and cider only — no lager. Regular free live music. A proper old-school London boozer.

name: Howling Hops Tank Bar
description: A brewery taproom serving beer straight from the tanks — as fresh as it gets. Industrial space in Hackney Wick with a lively weekend atmosphere.
tips: Beer served direct from the tank — doesn't get fresher. Hackney Wick is full of breweries to explore.

name: Pressure Drop Brewery
description: A popular Tottenham Hale taproom with excellent modern craft beer and a friendly, inclusive atmosphere. Regular food pop-ups and events.
address: Unit 6, Ashley House, Ashley Rd, London N17 9LZ
tips: One of London's best modern breweries. The taproom has regular food pop-ups. Worth the trip.

name: The Rake
description: A tiny craft beer bar at Borough Market with an astounding selection of rare and interesting beers. Small but perfectly formed.
tips: Right in Borough Market — perfect for a beer after browsing the food stalls. Tiny but the beer list is huge.

name: Mother Kelly's
description: A railway arch taproom in Bethnal Green with 23 taps of carefully curated craft beer and a bottle shop. Industrial chic with excellent taste.
tips: The tap list is always interesting. You can buy bottles to take away too. Great spot for craft beer lovers.

name: The Dove Freehouse
description: A quirky Broadway Market pub specialising in Belgian beer with an eclectic crowd and a beloved Sunday roast. A real Hackney institution.
tips: The Belgian beer selection is outstanding. Visit on Saturday when Broadway Market is in full swing.

name: The Royal Oak
description: A beautifully restored Victorian pub near Borough Market. Genuine Harvey's ales, traditional pub food, and an interior that feels unchanged for a century.
tips: Harvey's Sussex ales — rare in London. The restored Victorian interior is a gem. Proper pub atmosphere.

name: The Wenlock Arms
description: A legendary real ale pub saved from demolition by a community campaign. Rotating guest ales, free live jazz, and an authentic local atmosphere.
tips: Free live jazz on weekends. A real ale haven saved by the community. One of London's great honest pubs.

name: The Crown & Shuttle
description: A large Shoreditch pub with a fantastic outdoor area. Craft beers, pizzas, and a laid-back vibe away from the hipster intensity of the main drag.
tips: The outdoor terrace is one of the best in Shoreditch. Good pizza and a more relaxed alternative to nearby bars.

name: Cargo
description: A Shoreditch institution under the railway arches with live music, DJs, club nights, and a large outdoor terrace. Something different every night.
tips: Check the lineup — varies from live bands to DJ club nights. The outdoor area is great in summer.

name: XOYO
description: A highly respected Shoreditch club and live music venue known for its excellent sound system and curated DJ residencies. Two floors of music.
tips: The quarterly DJ residencies are excellent. Great sound system. Fridays and Saturdays are the main club nights.

name: Egg London
description: A multi-floor nightclub in King's Cross with an outdoor garden and terrace. Known for marathon weekend sessions and quality electronic music.
tips: The garden area is great for a breather between dancefloors. Weekend parties can go very late.

name: Ministry of Sound
description: One of the world's most famous nightclubs with a legendary sound system. Four rooms of music and a heritage stretching back to 1991.
tips: The sound system in the Box is extraordinary. Book tickets online in advance for big nights. Dress to dance.

name: Phonox
description: A Brixton club in the former venue known as Plan B. Top-quality sound, diverse programming from house to grime, and a brilliant atmosphere.
tips: The programming is varied and excellent. Check the lineup — different crowd depending on the night.

name: Corsica Studios
description: An underground Elephant & Castle club with two rooms and a superb Funktion-One sound system. A favourite of serious electronic music heads.
tips: The sound system is phenomenal. Dark, sweaty, and perfect for losing yourself in music.

name: Electric Brixton
description: A Grade II listed former cinema turned club and live music venue. Stunning Art Deco interior with a huge capacity and eclectic programming.
tips: The building is beautiful — a former cinema. Great for live gigs and club nights. Check the lineup.

name: Village Underground
description: A creative venue in converted Victorian railway arches topped with tube carriages. Live music, club nights, and cultural events in a unique space.
tips: Look for the tube carriages on the roof — iconic Shoreditch landmark. Great for live music and club nights.

name: Omeara
description: An intimate live music venue near London Bridge founded by Mumford & Sons' Ben Lovett. Excellent acoustics and a carefully curated lineup.
tips: Small venue means every gig feels intimate. Great for catching artists before they blow up.

name: The Lexington
description: An Islington pub and music venue with a lively Americana-themed bar downstairs and intimate live music room upstairs. Great bourbon selection.
tips: The upstairs venue is wonderfully intimate. Great bourbon and whiskey selection. Check the gig listings.

name: The Half Moon
description: A legendary Putney music pub where the Rolling Stones, U2, and Kate Bush have all played. Still hosting excellent live music in a proper pub setting.
tips: A historic music venue — the Stones played here. Still hosting great live music. Check the listings.

name: Bush Hall
description: A stunning Edwardian dance hall turned intimate music venue. Ornate plasterwork, chandeliers, and incredible acoustics for up to 350 people.
tips: The Edwardian interior is gorgeous. Intimate gigs in a beautiful setting. Check the listings.

name: The Windmill
description: A legendary Brixton grass-roots music venue that has launched countless bands. Tiny, sweaty, and absolutely essential for discovering new music.
tips: London's best grass-roots music venue. Catch bands before they're famous. Small, hot, and brilliant.

name: Union Chapel
description: A working church that doubles as one of London's most atmospheric live music venues. The acoustics and setting are extraordinary.
tips: Seeing a gig in a Gothic Revival church is unforgettable. The acoustics are phenomenal. Seated venue.

name: The Troubadour
description: A legendary Earls Court coffee house and music venue since 1954. Bob Dylan, Jimi Hendrix, and Adele have all performed in the basement club.
tips: A piece of music history — the basement club has hosted legends. Intimate and atmospheric.

name: KOKO
description: A stunning Victorian theatre in Camden, lavishly restored. Multiple floors of bars, dancefloors, and live music in one of London's most beautiful venues.
tips: Recently reopened after a massive restoration. The Victorian theatre interior is jaw-dropping. Multiple bars across different floors.

name: Dalston Superstore
description: A queer-centric bar and club in Dalston with art exhibitions, club nights, and a cafe by day. Diverse, creative, and always welcoming.
tips: Cafe by day, bar and club by night. The club nights are diverse and brilliant. Welcoming to everyone.

name: The Royal Vauxhall Tavern
description: A Grade II listed LGBTQ+ pub and performance venue with a legendary history. Drag, cabaret, and live music since the 1860s.
tips: Grade II listed as a venue of cultural importance. The Sunday social and drag shows are legendary.

name: The Yard
description: A relaxed LGBTQ+ bar in a courtyard off Rupert Street in Soho. Chilled atmosphere, good cocktails, and a lovely heated outdoor area.
tips: More relaxed than the main Soho LGBTQ+ bars. The courtyard is a lovely spot for a drink.

name: The Admiral Duncan
description: A historic Soho LGBTQ+ pub on Old Compton Street. A cornerstone of London's queer community with a lively, welcoming atmosphere.
tips: A historic and important venue for London's LGBTQ+ community. Lively atmosphere, especially on weekends.

name: The George & Dragon
description: A lively Shoreditch LGBTQ+ pub with drag nights, karaoke, and a friendly neighbourhood vibe. East London's alternative to Soho's gay scene.
tips: The drag nights are hilarious and the karaoke is legendary. Very friendly atmosphere.

name: The Greenwich Union
description: A craft beer pub in Greenwich specialising in Meantime Brewery beers. Bright, modern interior with a small garden and views towards the park.
tips: Great for a post-Greenwich Park drink. The craft beer selection is excellent. Nice garden in summer.

name: The Trafalgar Tavern
description: A grand Regency-era riverside pub in Greenwich with stunning Thames views. Dickens set a wedding feast here in Our Mutual Friend.
tips: The Thames views from the upstairs dining room are stunning. Great for Sunday roast with a river view.

name: The Cutty Sark Tavern
description: A beautiful Georgian riverside pub in Greenwich with a large terrace overlooking the Thames. Excellent ales and a genuinely historic atmosphere.
tips: The riverside terrace is one of London's best pub views. A short walk from the main Greenwich attractions.

name: The Old Brewery
description: A brewery, cafe, and bar inside the Old Royal Naval College in Greenwich. Brew their own beers in the stunning Painted Hall complex.
address: Old Royal Naval College, London SE10 9LW
tips: Set inside one of London's most beautiful buildings. Their own-brewed beers are good. Visit the Painted Hall too.

name: The Narrowboat
description: A charming canalside pub on Regent's Canal in Islington. Watch the narrowboats glide past while enjoying a pint on the waterside terrace.
tips: The canalside terrace is lovely on sunny days. Watch the narrowboats go through the lock.

name: The Scolt Head
description: A wonderful De Beauvoir neighbourhood pub with excellent food, a lovely garden, and a real community feel. Sunday roasts are outstanding.
tips: The Sunday roast is superb. The garden is a hidden gem. A proper neighbourhood local.

name: The Cat & Mutton
description: A stylish Broadway Market pub with DJs, a weekend crowd, and a Sunday roast that draws people from across London. A Hackney classic.
tips: Weekend DJs bring a lively crowd. The Sunday roast is legendary. Perfect on a Saturday market day.

name: The Royal Inn on the Park
description: A lovely Victoria Park pub with a heated terrace and excellent seasonal menu. A refined neighbourhood pub with a genuinely warm atmosphere.
tips: Perfect after a walk around Victoria Park. The food is consistently excellent.

name: The Camberwell Arms
description: A much-loved Camberwell gastropub with a daily-changing blackboard menu and an outstanding wine list. Unfussy food done brilliantly.
tips: The daily-changing menu is always interesting. The wine list is exceptional for a pub.

name: The Palmerston
description: A refined East Dulwich gastropub with an emphasis on seasonal British cooking. One of south London's best dining pubs.
tips: The seasonal British food is excellent. A refined dining experience in a relaxed pub setting.

name: Peckham Springs
description: A quirky Peckham bar in a railway arch with house-infused spirits, homemade mixers, and a vibrant atmosphere. Creative cocktails at accessible prices.
tips: The house-infused spirits are creative and fun. A good starting point for a Peckham night out.

name: Peckham Levels
description: A multi-storey car park converted into a creative community with bars, street food, co-working, and rooftop views. The bar has panoramic London views.
tips: Multiple food vendors and bars. The roof terrace has stunning sunset views. A real Peckham institution.

name: Prince of Wales
description: A Brixton rooftop bar institution with panoramic views, DJs, and a party atmosphere. Multiple floors and a legendary weekend vibe.
tips: The rooftop in summer is brilliant. DJs most weekends. A proper Brixton institution.

name: Brixton Village
description: A covered market arcade with numerous small bars and restaurants. From cocktail bars to wine spots to craft beer, all under one atmospheric roof.
tips: Multiple venues under one roof — bar hop within the market. Great food options too. Very atmospheric in the evening.

name: Lost in Brixton
description: A Brixton rooftop bar with a lively Latino-inspired atmosphere. Cocktails, tacos, and DJs with a colourful, festive decor.
tips: Lively atmosphere with Latin-inspired cocktails and food. The rooftop is great in summer.

name: The Old Queen's Head
description: A beautiful Islington pub in a Tudor-style building with DJs, comedy nights, and a packed weekend crowd. Great mix of pub and nightlife.
tips: Free entry to most events. DJ nights, comedy, and quiz nights. The building is gorgeous.

name: The Compton Arms
description: A tiny, hidden Islington pub down a backstreet that feels like a country village local. George Orwell described it as his ideal pub.
tips: George Orwell's inspiration for his essay on the ideal pub. Tiny, quiet, and utterly charming.

name: The Three Kings of Clerkenwell
description: An eccentric Clerkenwell pub with quirky decor, an excellent jukebox, and a friendly, bohemian crowd. A proper neighbourhood character pub.
tips: The jukebox is one of the best in London. Eccentric decor and a loyal local following.

name: The Auld Shillelagh
description: A legendary Stoke Newington Irish pub with live music, Gaelic football on the TV, and one of the best pub atmospheres in London.
address: 105 Stoke Newington Church St, London N16 0UD
tips: The best Irish pub in London. Live music sessions, GAA on the TV. Incredible atmosphere.

name: The Pineapple
description: A hidden residential-street pub saved from developers by the local community. Wonderful Thai food, a friendly crowd, and a lovely garden.
tips: Hidden on a residential street — worth seeking out. The Thai food is excellent and cheap.

name: The Dolphin
description: A Hackney institution that mixes art gallery, pub, and music venue. Rotating exhibitions, DJs, and a relaxed creative atmosphere.
tips: Check the art exhibitions — they change regularly. DJs on weekends. A real Hackney creative hub.

name: The Stag
description: A stylish Fleet Road pub in Hampstead with excellent food, craft beers, and a lovely front terrace. Popular with locals and walkers from the Heath.
tips: Great brunch spot on weekends. The terrace is lovely and it's perfect after a Heath walk.

name: The Old Ship
description: A Mare Street pub with one of Hackney's best beer gardens, regular DJ nights, and a friendly neighbourhood atmosphere. Great in summer.
tips: The beer garden is huge and perfect for summer. Regular DJ nights and quiz nights.

name: The Champion
description: A beautiful Victorian corner pub in Notting Hill with stunning original stained glass windows depicting sporting champions. Unique interior.
tips: The Victorian stained glass windows are museum-quality. Each one depicts a different sporting champion.

name: The Elgin
description: A grand Notting Hill pub on Ladbroke Grove with high ceilings, ornate decor, and a lively weekend atmosphere. DJs on weekends.
tips: The grand Victorian interior is impressive. Gets lively at weekends with DJs. Good for the Notting Hill Carnival area.

name: The Portobello Star
description: A cocktail bar and gin specialist on the famous Portobello Road with its own gin distillery. Masterclasses available in their Ginstitute upstairs.
tips: Book a gin masterclass at the Ginstitute upstairs — you blend your own gin to take home.

name: Trailer Happiness
description: A retro tiki bar in a Notting Hill basement with tropical cocktails, rum punches, and a Polynesian vibe. Kitsch, fun, and excellent drinks.
tips: Kitschy tiki decor and excellent rum cocktails. Great for a fun night out. Gets busy at weekends.

name: The Cross Keys
description: A charming Chelsea pub covered in flowers that rivals the Churchill Arms for photogenic appeal. Cosy interior and friendly atmosphere.
tips: The flower-covered exterior is gorgeous — great for photos. A quieter, more local Chelsea pub.

name: The Builders Arms
description: A stylish Chelsea gastropub on a pretty residential street. Excellent food, good wine, and a smart but relaxed neighbourhood atmosphere.
tips: Surprisingly relaxed for Chelsea. Good wine list and the food is consistently strong.

name: The Pig's Ear
description: A handsome Chelsea pub with a fine dining restaurant upstairs and a traditional pub bar downstairs. Smart without being stuffy.
tips: Two experiences in one — casual drinks downstairs, fine dining upstairs. Great for Chelsea King's Road.

name: The Atlas
description: A popular Fulham gastropub with an excellent Mediterranean-influenced menu, good wines, and a lovely enclosed garden. A neighbourhood favourite.
tips: The Mediterranean-influenced food is excellent. The garden is a lovely sun trap.

name: The Brown Cow
description: A friendly Fulham pub right by the Thames with excellent ales and a large garden. Perfect for riverside walks and family-friendly daytime drinks.
tips: Close to the Thames path — perfect after a riverside walk. The garden is big and dog-friendly.

name: The Duke of Cambridge
description: The UK's first certified organic pub, serving organic ales, wines, and seasonal British food. Everything from the meat to the cleaning products is organic.
tips: Britain's first organic pub. The seasonal menu changes daily. Great for ethical eating and drinking.

name: The Hemingford Arms
description: A hidden Islington pub covered in flowers with a secret garden that feels miles from London. Cosy, romantic, and full of character.
tips: The flower-covered exterior and secret garden are magical. One of London's most romantic neighbourhood pubs.

name: The Prince Regent
description: A characterful Marylebone pub near Regent's Park with a friendly atmosphere and well-kept ales. A genuine local in an area dominated by restaurants.
tips: A proper local pub on an otherwise upmarket high street. Good ales and a friendly crowd.

name: The Barley Mow
description: A traditional Marylebone pub with original Victorian features and a small but perfectly formed interior. A hidden gem near Paddington Street Gardens.
tips: A proper old-fashioned pub experience. Cosy and characterful. Near the great Paddington Street Gardens.

name: The Marylebone
description: A smart Marylebone cocktail bar and restaurant in a beautifully converted space. Sophisticated cocktails and a refined after-work atmosphere.
tips: Sophisticated cocktails in a smart setting. Good for a refined evening out on Marylebone High Street.

name: The Star Tavern
description: A hidden Belgravia mews pub where the Great Train Robbery was reportedly planned. Outstanding Fuller's ales in an upmarket village setting.
tips: The Great Train Robbery was reportedly planned here. Hidden in a gorgeous Belgravia mews.

name: The Guinea
description: A tiny, traditional Mayfair pub with a legendary steakhouse restaurant attached. Outstanding steak pies and excellent Young's ales.
tips: The steak and kidney pie is legendary. A proper pub in the heart of Mayfair — rare and precious.

name: The Red Lion Mayfair
description: A classic Mayfair pub on a quiet side street with Victorian-era wood panelling and a convivial after-work atmosphere. Proper ales in a posh neighbourhood.
tips: A proper traditional pub in the heart of Mayfair. Great after-work atmosphere with City types.

name: The Punchbowl
description: A stylish Mayfair pub formerly owned by Guy Ritchie and David Beckham. Georgian decor, fine ales, and an upmarket pub food menu.
tips: Formerly celebrity-owned. The Georgian interior is very smart. Upmarket pub food is excellent.

name: Tayēr + Elementary
description: A split cocktail bar in Old Street — Elementary for casual standing drinks, Tayēr for serious seated cocktail experiences. Both outstanding.
tips: Two bars in one — Elementary for quick drinks, Tayēr for the full experience. Both are excellent.

name: Coupette
description: A French-inspired cocktail bar in Bethnal Green known for its apple-brandy focus and innovative techniques. Relaxed atmosphere with world-class drinks.
tips: Try the Champagne Piña Colada — their signature. The Calvados and apple brandy selection is unmatched.

name: Seed Library
description: A cocktail bar inside The Langham hotel's former wine cellar focused on seeds, grains, and botanical ingredients. Unique concept with stunning results.
address: The Langham, 1C Portland Pl, London W1B 1JA
tips: The seed-based concept is genuinely unique. Each cocktail tells a botanical story. Book ahead.

name: The Blind Pig
description: A hidden cocktail bar above Social Eating House in Soho, accessed through an unmarked door. Literary-themed cocktails in a sophisticated speakeasy setting.
tips: Look for the unmarked door above the restaurant. The literary-themed cocktails are very creative.

name: Evans & Peel Detective Agency
description: A Prohibition-era speakeasy disguised as a detective agency. Ring the buzzer, present your 'case', and be ushered through a secret door into the bar.
tips: Book ahead and prepare your 'case' — it's part of the fun. The theatrical entrance is memorable.

name: Purl London
description: A Prohibition-inspired basement bar in Marylebone with molecular cocktails, smoke-filled bubbles, and theatrical presentations. Inventive and fun.
tips: The molecular cocktails are theatrical and fun. Great for special occasions and impressing dates.

name: Opium Cocktails & Dim Sum Parlour
description: A hidden Chinatown cocktail bar accessed through an unmarked door and up a narrow staircase. Oriental-inspired cocktails across three themed rooms.
tips: Hidden above Chinatown — look for the jade door. Three floors of different experiences. Book ahead.

name: The Blues Kitchen Brixton
description: Live blues, soul, and rock music every night in a Brixton venue with American BBQ food and bourbon cocktails. Free entry most nights.
tips: Free live music most nights. The bourbon selection is excellent and the BBQ is proper.

name: The Blues Kitchen Camden
description: The Camden outpost of the Blues Kitchen chain with live music every night. American BBQ, craft bourbon, and a juke joint atmosphere.
tips: Free live music seven nights a week. Great bourbon cocktails and BBQ. Perfect Camden night out.

name: Green Note
description: A tiny, intimate live music venue in Camden focusing on folk, world, and acoustic music. Only 50 seats, creating an extraordinarily intimate experience.
tips: Only 50 seats — incredibly intimate. Book ahead. World-class folk and acoustic acts.

name: Vortex Jazz Club
description: A respected Dalston jazz venue showcasing cutting-edge contemporary jazz, improvised music, and experimental performances. Intimate and artistically adventurous.
tips: For adventurous jazz fans. The programming is cutting-edge. Small venue with great sightlines.

name: O2 Forum Kentish Town
description: A beautiful Art Deco live music venue with great acoustics and a 2,300 capacity. Catches artists at an exciting point in their career.
tips: Great size venue — big enough for atmosphere, small enough to see the stage. The Art Deco interior is lovely.

name: The Bill Murray
description: A pub and comedy venue in Islington named after the actor. Nightly comedy shows, craft beer, and a friendly community atmosphere.
tips: Comedy shows most nights — check the listings. Named after the actor but unaffiliated. Great local pub.

name: The White Hart
description: A local pub near Waterloo station with a big screen for sports, regular quiz nights, and a friendly neighbourhood atmosphere despite its central location.
tips: Good for watching sport before or after events at the South Bank. Quiz nights are popular.

name: The Shipwright's Arms
description: A cosy traditional pub near London Bridge and the Shard. Real ales, friendly staff, and a welcome respite from the corporate surroundings.
tips: A proper traditional pub in the shadow of the Shard. Cash-friendly and unpretentious.

name: The Market Porter
description: A Borough Market pub famous for opening at 6am for the market traders. Outstanding rotating selection of real ales and a historic interior.
tips: Opens at 6am for market workers. The ale selection is incredible — often 10+ guest ales. Right at Borough Market.

name: The Woolpack
description: A proper Bermondsey local with craft beer, regular events, and a lovely garden. A friendly neighbourhood pub away from the tourist trail.
tips: On the increasingly trendy Bermondsey Street. Good craft beer selection and a friendly local vibe.

name: Bermondsey Arts Club
description: A Prohibition-style cocktail bar hidden behind a launderette facade. Ring the buzzer and enter through the washing machine door. Excellent cocktails.
tips: Hidden behind a launderette — ring the buzzer. The entrance through the 'washing machine' is brilliant.

name: The Dead Dolls House
description: A gothic-themed cocktail bar in Islington with a dark, theatrical atmosphere. Ornate Victorian decor, taxidermy, and creative cocktails.
tips: The gothic decor is spectacular. Great for Halloween or anyone who loves dark, theatrical aesthetics.

name: Counting House
description: A Wetherspoons in a magnificent former NatWest banking hall in the City. Stunning domed ceiling, chandeliers, and absurdly cheap pints.
tips: Another stunning Wetherspoons conversion. Look up at the domed ceiling. Cheapest pints in the Square Mile.

name: The Liberty Bounds
description: A large Wetherspoons near the Tower of London with history-themed decor and views of the castle. Budget-friendly with good food options.
tips: Great value near the Tower of London. Named after the historic liberty boundaries of the Tower.

name: The Captain Kidd
description: A Thames-side pub in Wapping named after the notorious pirate. Excellent river views from the terrace, real ales, and a nautical atmosphere.
tips: Named after the pirate who was executed nearby. The river terrace is lovely. Near the Prospect of Whitby.

name: The Town of Ramsgate
description: A 15th-century Wapping pub where Judge Jeffreys was captured fleeing to escape to France. Atmospheric riverside setting with a dark history.
tips: One of several historic Wapping riverside pubs. The alley next door once led to Execution Dock.

name: The Gun
description: A beautifully restored riverside pub in Docklands with views of the O2 dome. Lord Nelson reportedly had a secret love tryst here.
tips: The riverside terrace with O2 views is stunning. Nelson's alleged secret meeting spot. Excellent food.

name: The Lord Nelson
description: A traditional corner pub in Southwark with well-kept ales and a friendly local atmosphere. A proper no-frills pub near the Old Vic.
tips: A proper no-frills local pub. Good for an authentic London boozer experience.

name: The Palm Tree
description: A legendary East End pub standing alone in Mile End Park. Live jazz at weekends, an old-school atmosphere, and one of London's most unique settings.
tips: Standing alone in the park — an incredible setting. Live jazz at weekends. A true East End institution.

name: The Pride of Spitalfields
description: A tiny, authentic East End boozer with a resident cat, real ales, and zero pretension. One of the few remaining old-school pubs in gentrified Spitalfields.
tips: Look for the resident cat. A proper old-school East End pub. No frills, just a great honest boozer.

name: The Old Blue Last
description: A legendary Shoreditch pub owned by Vice magazine. Free live music and DJ nights discovering tomorrow's indie stars. Always buzzing.
tips: Free live music most nights — catch bands before they blow up. Always busy and always interesting.

name: The Approach Tavern
description: A Bethnal Green pub with a contemporary art gallery upstairs. Great ales downstairs, thought-provoking art upstairs. A unique combination.
tips: The gallery upstairs is free and features emerging artists. Drink, then browse. A Bethnal Green institution.

name: 69 Colebrooke Row
description: A tiny, perfect cocktail bar run by award-winning bartender Tony Conigliaro. Only 28 seats, no sign outside. Precise, innovative cocktails.
tips: No sign — just the number 69. Only 28 seats so book ahead. Every cocktail is a masterwork.

name: The Old Fountain
description: A proper Old Street real ale pub with an outstanding selection of craft beers and guest ales. Friendly, unfussy, and run by real beer enthusiasts.
tips: The ale selection is exceptional and constantly rotating. Staff really know their beer.

name: The Windmill
description: A Young's pub on a quiet Mayfair street with excellent pies and a cosy, wood-panelled interior. A proper pub oasis in London's most exclusive area.
tips: The pies are famous. A proper pub in the heart of Mayfair — surprisingly unstuffy.

name: The Fellow
description: A smart gastropub near King's Cross with canal views, excellent food, and a sophisticated atmosphere. Popular with post-work drinkers.
tips: Near the canal with a nice terrace. Good food and wine. Popular with the creative King's Cross crowd.

name: Ridley Road Market Bar
description: A lively Dalston bar with a retro Caribbean feel, strong rum cocktails, and regular DJ nights. Colourful, friendly, and always fun.
tips: Great rum cocktails and a fun Caribbean vibe. Regular DJs and a loyal local crowd.

name: Birthdays
description: A popular Dalston bar and basement club with eclectic DJ nights. A key part of east London's nightlife scene with always-interesting programming.
tips: The basement club nights are varied and interesting. Check listings — different crowd every night.

name: The Dog & Bell
description: A classic Deptford pub with a secluded garden, real ales, and a warm community atmosphere. One of south-east London's best traditional pubs.
tips: A proper local pub in increasingly cool Deptford. Good ales, nice garden, friendly atmosphere.

name: Little Nan's Bar
description: A delightfully kitsch cocktail bar styled like your nan's living room. Mismatched furniture, bric-a-brac, and cocktails served in teapots.
tips: Cocktails served in teapots at your nan's house. The kitsch decor is genuinely hilarious. Great for groups.

name: The Telegraph
description: A popular Brixton Hill pub with a large garden, weekly pub quiz, and a strong community atmosphere. Great craft beer selection.
tips: Great garden and a loyal local crowd. The weekly quiz is popular. Good craft beer selection.

name: Effra Social
description: A Brixton venue combining pub, club, and live music. Regular DJ nights playing funk, soul, jazz, and reggae. Free entry most nights.
tips: Free entry most nights. The DJ nights are brilliant — funk, soul, reggae. A true Brixton institution.

name: The Half Moon
description: A lovely Herne Hill pub with a famous large garden. Regular live music, quiz nights, and a genuine neighbourhood feel beloved by locals.
tips: The garden is one of south London's best. Regular live music and a great community pub.

name: The White Horse
description: Known as the 'Sloaney Pony', this Parsons Green pub has an exceptional beer selection, regular beer festivals, and a huge terrace on the green.
tips: The beer selection is world-class. Regular beer festivals and tastings. The terrace overlooking the green is lovely.

name: The Cat's Back
description: An eccentric Wandsworth pub packed with vintage curiosities, old radios, and random treasures. Regular quiz nights and a unique atmosphere.
tips: Full of weird and wonderful vintage objects. The quiz is great. A truly eccentric local.

name: The Duke's Head
description: A grand Young's pub right on the Thames at Putney Bridge. Excellent for watching the Boat Race, with a large riverside terrace.
tips: Right at the Boat Race start line. The riverside terrace is excellent. Great for watching rowers.

name: The Ship
description: A large Young's pub with one of London's best riverside beer gardens. Views of the Thames, BBQ in summer, and regular events.
tips: The riverside garden with BBQ is one of London's best summer spots. Huge and family-friendly during the day.

name: Four Thieves
description: A Battersea pub with its own microbrewery, VR gaming, retro arcades, and a pub quiz. More of an entertainment complex than a traditional pub.
tips: VR gaming, retro arcades, and their own brewed beers. Not your average pub. Great for groups.

name: The Magic Garden
description: A lively Battersea Rise pub with a huge beer garden, DJs on weekends, and a fun, youthful atmosphere. One of Battersea's most popular spots.
tips: The beer garden is huge and gets packed on sunny weekends. DJs create a festival atmosphere.

name: The Sun
description: A large Clapham pub with a spacious garden, good food, and regular events. A reliable neighbourhood pub on the edge of Clapham Common.
tips: Near Clapham Common. The garden is great in summer. Good food and a reliable local choice.

name: Infernos
description: Clapham's legendary cheesy nightclub. Three floors of pop, cheese, and party classics. Fancy dress encouraged. It's terrible and brilliant in equal measure.
tips: Embrace the cheese. Fancy dress nights are legendary. It's an experience everyone should have once.

name: Aqua Shard
description: A bar on the 31st floor of the Shard with vertigo-inducing views across London. Cocktails with a panoramic backdrop of the city skyline.
address: Level 31, The Shard, 31 St Thomas St, London SE1 9RY
tips: No booking fee — just turn up. The views are astonishing. Smart casual dress code.

name: The Portobello Gold
description: A long-established Notting Hill pub and restaurant on Portobello Road. Live music, good food, and a tropical roof terrace with a retractable roof.
tips: The conservatory-style roof terrace is a hidden gem. Regular live music. Perfect for Portobello Market day.

name: Mr Fogg's Residence
description: A theatrical cocktail bar designed as the home of Phileas Fogg. Every surface is crammed with Victorian exploration memorabilia. Immersive and fun.
tips: Book ahead. The decor is incredible — truly immersive. Each room tells a different chapter of Fogg's story.

name: The Churchill Bar & Terrace
description: An elegant cocktail bar in the Hyatt Regency, themed around Churchill with war-time memorabilia and cigar terrace. Sophisticated and atmospheric.
tips: The Churchill theme is elegant. The terrace is lovely. Smart dress required.

name: The Jolly Butchers
description: A Stoke Newington craft beer pub with an ever-changing selection of rare and interesting beers. Knowledgeable staff and a passionate beer crowd.
address: 204 Stoke Newington High St, London N16 7HU
tips: The craft beer selection is outstanding and always changing. Staff really know their stuff.

name: The Chesham Arms
description: A community-saved Hackney pub that fought off developers. Simple, unpretentious, with a lovely garden and a strong sense of community spirit.
tips: Saved from developers by the community. Simple, honest, and welcoming. The garden is lovely.

name: The Clapton Hart
description: A large Clapton pub on the high street with a sprawling interior, craft beers, sourdough pizza, and a friendly neighbourhood crowd.
tips: Good pizza and craft beer. Spacious and relaxed. A good starting point for exploring Clapton.

name: The London Particular
description: A cosy New Cross cocktail bar in a converted Victorian shop front. Intimate, candlelit, with creative cocktails and a neighbourhood following.
tips: Named after the London fog. Cosy and candlelit. A surprisingly great cocktail bar in New Cross.

name: The King's Arms
description: A quirky Waterloo pub known for its spectacularly eccentric garden decor including mannequins and fairy lights. A true London original.
tips: Roupell Street is one of London's prettiest streets. The pub's garden decor is hilariously eccentric.

name: The MCC Tavern at Lord's
description: A pub at the world's most famous cricket ground. Watch cricket from the terrace while enjoying a pint. A must for sports fans.
address: Lord's Cricket Ground, St John's Wood Rd, London NW8 8QN
tips: Open on match days. Watch cricket from the terrace with a pint. The home of cricket.

name: The Warrington
description: A magnificent Art Nouveau pub in Maida Vale with a stunning interior featuring a painted ceiling, ornate plasterwork, and marble columns.
tips: The Art Nouveau interior is jaw-dropping. Originally a hotel, the ceramic and glass work is museum quality.

name: The Red Lion Westminster
description: The closest pub to 10 Downing Street, frequented by politicians and civil servants. A historic Westminster institution with division bells.
tips: You might spot an MP. The closest pub to Downing Street. Division bells ring when there's a vote.

name: The Flask Hampstead
description: A charming 18th-century pub in the heart of Hampstead Village with a large garden. A favourite of locals, walkers, and literary types.
tips: Named after the flasks used to bottle the Hampstead spa waters. The garden is lovely. Great after a Heath walk.

name: The Lock Tavern
description: A Camden Lock pub with a roof terrace overlooking the canal market. Live music, DJs, and a great mix of tourists and locals.
tips: The roof terrace overlooking the market is brilliant. Live music and DJs. A Camden essential.

name: The Hawley Arms
description: A legendary Camden pub that was Amy Winehouse's local. Rebuilt after a devastating fire in 2008. Live music, DJs, and a rock'n'roll atmosphere.
tips: Amy Winehouse's local pub. Rebuilt after a 2008 fire. Live music and a genuine Camden atmosphere.

name: The Spread Eagle
description: London's first fully vegan pub in Camden, serving plant-based food and ethical drinks. Regular events, DJs, and a cinema upstairs.
tips: London's first vegan pub — everything is plant-based. They also have a cinema upstairs. Cool concept.

name: Homeboy
description: An Irish-inspired cocktail bar in Islington with innovative whiskey cocktails and a relaxed, convivial atmosphere. Modern Irish hospitality at its best.
tips: The Irish whiskey cocktails are outstanding. Warm, friendly service. Try the Irish Coffee.

name: The Pig and Butcher
description: A handsome Islington gastropub in a former butcher's shop. They butcher their own meat on site and the steaks are outstanding.
tips: They butcher their own meat on site. The steaks are exceptional. A serious food pub.

name: The Garage
description: A legendary Islington live music venue since 1993. Has hosted Oasis, Radiohead, and countless others. Intimate, sweaty, and essential.
tips: A piece of music history. Small enough that every gig feels intimate. Check the listings.

name: A Bar with Shapes for a Name
description: A Hackney Downs cocktail bar named only by geometric shapes on the signage. Creative cocktails, friendly service, and a neighbourhood feel.
tips: Look for the shapes on the sign — no words. Great cocktails in a neighbourhood setting.

name: The Victoria
description: A stunning Victorian pub in Dalston with original features, a roof terrace, and excellent food. One of east London's most handsome pub buildings.
tips: The building is gorgeous. The roof terrace is a bonus. Good food and a well-curated drinks list.

name: The Duke of Edinburgh
description: A large Brixton pub with a huge garden, regular DJ nights, and a diverse local crowd. A Brixton staple for nights out and lazy weekends.
tips: The garden is huge. Regular DJs and events. A proper Brixton local with a diverse crowd.

name: Studio 9294
description: A Hackney Wick warehouse venue with a canal-side terrace, DJs, and an industrial-creative atmosphere. Part of the Hackney Wick creative scene.
tips: Canal-side setting in creative Hackney Wick. Check the events listings — varied programming.

name: The Crown
description: A grand Islington pub on Cloudesley Road with an impressive interior, good food, and a nice garden. A reliable neighbourhood gastropub.
tips: Good food and a lovely garden. A step up from the average pub. Quiet enough for conversation.

name: The Angel
description: A riverside pub in Rotherhithe with a trapdoor to the Thames. Atmospheric and historic with connections to the Mayflower voyage.
tips: Ask about the famous trapdoor above the Thames. Atmospheric riverside setting off the tourist trail.

name: The Crooked Well
description: A stylish Camberwell gastropub with seasonal food, excellent cocktails, and a smart-casual atmosphere. One of south London's best dining pubs.
tips: Named after a historic local well. The seasonal food is very good. Great cocktail list for a pub.

name: El Vino
description: A legendary Fleet Street wine bar that was the haunt of journalists and barristers for decades. Old-school atmosphere and an excellent wine list.
tips: A piece of Fleet Street journalism history. The wine list is excellent. Old-school atmosphere.

name: Balham Bowls Club
description: A bar in a converted bowling green pavilion in Balham with a large outdoor space. Cocktails, food, and a relaxed south London atmosphere.
tips: The large outdoor area is great in summer. Cocktails and food in a relaxed setting. Very Balham.

name: The Bedford
description: A grand Balham pub famous for its Banana Cabaret comedy club, live music, and multiple bars across a beautiful Victorian building.
tips: The Banana Cabaret comedy nights on Fridays and Saturdays are brilliant. The building is stunning.

name: The Windsor Castle Marylebone
description: A charming Marylebone pub with separate wood-panelled rooms, each with their own entrance. Traditional and atmospheric with real character.
tips: The separate rooms each have their own character. A proper traditional pub with great atmosphere.

name: The Exmouth Arms
description: A popular Clerkenwell pub on Exmouth Market with a heated terrace, craft beers, and a buzzy atmosphere. Perfect for people-watching.
tips: Great terrace for people-watching on Exmouth Market. Good craft beer selection.

name: The Fox & Anchor
description: A beautifully restored Art Nouveau pub in Smithfield with early-morning opening for market workers. Famous fry-ups and excellent ales.
tips: Opens at 7am for market workers. The Art Nouveau tiles are stunning. Famous for its fry-up breakfast.

name: The Betsey Trotwood
description: A Clerkenwell pub named after a Dickens character with a basement live music venue. Regular gigs, comedy, and spoken word events.
tips: The basement hosts great live music, comedy, and spoken word. Named after a Dickens character.

name: The Sekforde
description: A refined Clerkenwell gastropub with an extensive sherry list, Spanish-influenced tapas, and a smart but relaxed atmosphere.
tips: The sherry list is exceptional. Spanish-influenced tapas are excellent. A sophisticated neighbourhood gem.

name: The Green Man
description: A traditional Putney Heath pub on the edge of the common with a large garden. Popular with walkers and families during the day.
tips: On the edge of Putney Heath — great after a walk. The large garden is perfect for summer.

name: The Ivy House
description: London's first co-operatively owned pub, saved by the community from developers. Live music, comedy, and a genuine community spirit.
tips: London's first community-owned pub. Regular live music and events. A real grassroots success story.

name: The Sun and Doves
description: A friendly Camberwell pub with a large garden, pub quiz, and regular DJs. A south London local with a creative, diverse crowd.
tips: Good garden and a diverse, friendly crowd. Quiz nights are popular. A proper south London local.

name: The Three Stags
description: A Victorian pub near Kennington Park with good ales and traditional pub food. A local favourite with a no-frills, honest atmosphere.
tips: A proper neighbourhood local. No frills, just good beer and friendly faces.

name: Oblix at The Shard
description: A bar and restaurant on the 32nd floor of The Shard with panoramic London views. Live music and cocktails with a breathtaking backdrop.
address: Level 32, The Shard, 31 St Thomas St, London SE1 9RY
tips: The views from the 32nd floor are staggering. Live music in the evenings. Smart casual dress code.

name: Radio Rooftop Bar
description: A rooftop bar at ME London hotel with views of the Thames, Somerset House, and the South Bank. Mediterranean-inspired cocktails and nibbles.
address: ME London, 336-337 The Strand, London WC2R 1HA
tips: Stunning views of the Thames and Somerset House. Book ahead for terrace tables.

name: Boisdale of Canary Wharf
description: A cigar terrace, whisky bar, and live jazz venue in Canary Wharf. Over 1,000 whiskies and nightly jazz performances. Sophisticated and unique.
tips: Over 1,000 whiskies and nightly live jazz. The cigar terrace is one of London's best. Smart dress.

name: The Ledger Building
description: A waterside gastropub in a converted Docklands warehouse. Craft beers, excellent food, and views over the old docks.
tips: Beautiful dockside setting. Good food and craft beer. A welcome change from the corporate Canary Wharf vibe.

name: The Gin Palace
description: A moody, candlelit Islington bar specialising in gin with a huge selection of botanicals. Atmospheric Victorian-style decor and serious gin expertise.
tips: The gin selection is enormous. Candlelit and atmospheric. Staff are very knowledgeable about gin.

name: The Earl of Essex
description: A quirky Islington pub with craft beers, board games, and a cosy atmosphere. Dog-friendly with regular quiz nights and a loyal following.
tips: Board games, quiz nights, and dogs welcome. A proper cosy local.

name: P. Franco
description: A tiny Clapton wine bar and bottle shop with a constantly changing menu of natural wines. Counter dining with guest chefs. Incredibly popular.
tips: Tiny and always packed. Excellent natural wines. Guest chefs rotate regularly. Worth the wait.

name: The King Charles I
description: A traditional King's Cross pub with good ales, a snug atmosphere, and a welcome contrast to the area's modern developments.
tips: A traditional boozer in the midst of King's Cross regeneration. Unpretentious and friendly.

name: The Old Bell Tavern
description: Built by Sir Christopher Wren in 1678 as a hostelry for workers rebuilding St Bride's Church after the Great Fire. One of Fleet Street's oldest pubs.
tips: Built by Wren himself. The upstairs dining room is quieter. Right next to St Bride's Church.

name: The Phoenix
description: A Soho institution on Charing Cross Road popular with the theatre crowd. Friendly atmosphere and a perfect pre- or post-show pint.
tips: Popular with the theatre crowd from nearby West End venues. A proper Soho local.

name: The Coach & Horses
description: A legendary Soho pub famous as the drinking den of journalist Jeffrey Bernard. Now London's first vegetarian pub. Steeped in bohemian history.
tips: Jeffrey Bernard's legendary haunt. Now vegetarian. The Private Eye lunch is a piece of Soho history.

name: Ye Olde Watling
description: A historic City pub built in 1668 using timbers from ships broken up after the Great Fire. Named after the old Roman road of Watling Street.
tips: Built with ship timbers after the Great Fire. Named after the Roman road. A real piece of City history.

name: Dirty Dick's
description: A historic pub near Liverpool Street named after Nathaniel Bentley, an 18th-century dandy who became a recluse. Atmospheric cellar bar downstairs.
tips: Named after a real 18th-century eccentric. The cellar bar is atmospheric. Right near Liverpool Street station.

name: The Salisbury
description: A magnificent Victorian gin palace on St Martin's Lane with stunning cut glass, bronze nymphs, and Art Nouveau light fittings. A visual masterpiece.
tips: The Victorian interior is jaw-dropping. Bronze nymphs hold the light fittings. Perfect for pre-theatre drinks.

name: The Argyll Arms
description: A beautiful Victorian pub opposite Oxford Circus Tube with ornate etched glass partitions and a grand interior. A calm oasis amid the shopping madness.
tips: The etched glass partitions are stunning Victorian survivors. A surprisingly peaceful escape from Oxford Circus chaos.

name: The Museum Tavern
description: A characterful pub directly opposite the British Museum where Karl Marx reportedly drank while researching Das Kapital. Traditional Victorian interior.
tips: Karl Marx drank here while writing in the British Museum reading room. Perfect post-museum pint.

name: The Antelope
description: A charming Belgravia pub dating from 1827 on a pretty mews street. Cosy interior with panelled walls and a traditional atmosphere in one of London's poshest areas.
tips: A proper old-fashioned pub in posh Belgravia. The upstairs dining room is a hidden gem.

name: The Gibson
description: An acclaimed cocktail bar in Shoreditch from the team behind Oriole and Nightjar. Innovative drinks served in a sleek, intimate setting with a focus on pickled garnishes.
tips: Famous for its house-pickled garnishes. Book ahead. From the Nightjar team so expect excellence.

name: Scout
description: A sustainable cocktail bar in Hackney that uses every part of every ingredient. Inventive, eco-conscious cocktails in a relaxed neighbourhood setting.
tips: Zero-waste approach means incredibly creative flavour combinations. Every ingredient is used fully.

name: Below Stone Nest
description: A cocktail bar in the basement of a former Welsh chapel on Shaftesbury Avenue. Atmospheric stone walls, creative cocktails, and a unique setting.
tips: Hidden beneath a former Welsh chapel. The stone vaulted ceiling creates an amazing atmosphere.

name: Experimental Cocktail Club
description: A Parisian-style speakeasy in Chinatown hidden behind an unmarked door. Creative cocktails in a dimly lit, intimate space across multiple rooms.
tips: Ring the doorbell to enter. The Parisian-style decor is lovely. Book for weekends.

name: The Remedy
description: A cosy wine bar in Fitzrovia with an emphasis on natural and organic wines. Relaxed atmosphere with sharing plates and knowledgeable staff.
tips: Great natural wine selection with helpful staff. The sharing plates pair beautifully.

name: Bar Douro
description: A Portuguese wine bar near London Bridge with an outstanding selection of wines from the Douro Valley. Beautiful azulejo tiles and excellent petiscos.
address: Arch 35B, 85B Southwark Bridge Rd, London SE1 0NQ
tips: The Portuguese wines are exceptional. Try the petiscos sharing plates. The azulejo tiled counter is beautiful.

name: 10 Cases
description: A tiny Covent Garden wine bar with only 10 wines at any time, each limited to 10 cases. Simple French bistro food and a buzzy, intimate atmosphere.
tips: Only 10 wines at a time, each limited to 10 cases. The selection changes constantly. Tiny so arrive early.

name: Vagabond Wines
description: A self-pour wine bar with card-operated dispensing machines offering over 100 wines by the glass. Educational and fun with a modern approach to wine tasting.
tips: Self-pour machines let you taste over 100 wines. Load a card and explore. Great for learning about wine.

name: Berry Bros. & Rudd
description: Britain's oldest wine and spirits merchant, trading since 1698 from the same St James's premises. Their cellar bar offers extraordinary wine tastings and events.
tips: Trading since 1698. The Napoleon Cellar events are extraordinary. Book a tasting for a special occasion.

name: Roof East
description: A rooftop bar in Stratford with activities including crazy golf, cricket nets, and screenings. Panoramic views of the Olympic Park.
address: Stratford Multi-Storey Car Park, Great Eastern Rd, London E15 1BB
tips: Activities, drinks, and views of the Olympic Park. Open seasonally. Book activities in advance.

name: Boundary Rooftop
description: A Mediterranean-inspired rooftop bar and restaurant in Shoreditch with a retractable roof. Elegant setting with good cocktails and food year-round.
tips: The retractable roof means it works in all weather. Book ahead for sunset tables.

name: Dalston Roof Park
description: A community rooftop space in Dalston with a bar, DJs, and panoramic views. Summer pop-up with a sustainable, creative ethos.
tips: Open in summer only. Community-run with a great atmosphere. DJs and events on weekends.

name: BrewDog Shoreditch
description: The Shoreditch outpost of the Scottish craft beer chain with a huge selection of their own brews plus guest taps. Industrial decor and a lively crowd.
tips: Huge tap list including rare limited editions. Good burgers too. Multiple locations across London.

name: Fourpure Brewing Co.
description: A Bermondsey Beer Mile taproom with a wide range of craft beers brewed on site. Spacious industrial space with street food on weekends.
address: 22 Bermondsey Trading Estate, Rotherhithe New Rd, London SE16 3LL
tips: Part of the Bermondsey Beer Mile. Spacious taproom with street food on Saturdays.

name: Partizan Brewing
description: A highly regarded Bermondsey brewery with beautiful label art and excellent beers. Their taproom is a key stop on the Bermondsey Beer Mile.
tips: Known for striking label artwork. Open Saturdays on the Beer Mile. Excellent saisons and pale ales.

name: Anspach & Hobday
description: A Bermondsey Beer Mile brewery known for their porter and dark beers. The taproom serves the full range fresh from the tanks.
